newsitem.title: ITALY: Dini party to present Italy "Euro-tax" alternative. [CORRECTED 13:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Dini party to present Italy "Euro-tax" alternative. [CORRECTED 13:40 GMT]

text.p: Italian Renewal, the centrist political party led by Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini, will present an alternative to the government's planned "Euro-tax" on Wednesday, a spokeswoman said.

She said the party, a member of Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left (corrects from centre-right) coalition, would hold a news conference at 1430 GMT to outline its proposal. She had no further details.
Dini told reporters at the Senate earlier that the party's proposal was intended to overcome controversial aspects of the Euro-tax and to "share out the sacrifices a bit more equally".
His party has expressed reservations about how the measures will affect the self-employed.

The one-off levy planned for next year is a key element of the 62.5 trillion lire ($41.3 billion) budget. The tax is due to raise 12.5 trillion lire and help Italy make the grade as a founder member of a European single currency due in 1999.
Labour Minister Tiziano Treu said earlier the government was willing to revise details of the Euro-tax as long as the amount of revenue it was intended to raise was not altered.
Treu said the offer was intended as an olive branch to the centre-right Freedom Alliance, which has bitterly attacked the provisions and the thrust of Prodi's 1997 austerity budget.
